summary: Former CCC-staffed fire tower site on the Ozark National Forest, now Fairview Campground; no build or removal dates found.

facts.status_note: Described as a former fire tower; the Fairview Campground now sits on its site

staffing.status: Formerly staffed by members of the Civilian Conservation Corps while the tower operated

access.note: Fee campground ($7 per day) with a parking area, per a hiking-club page. That page's latest note is a 2014 proposal to decommission the campground.

visit.trail_note: Campground parking area is the access point for the Ozark Highlands Trail

evidence.supports: Campground sits at the site of a former fire tower, which was staffed by CCC members during its operation
evidence.quote: Fairview Campground is located at the site of a former fire tower previously staffed by members of the CCC (Civilian Conservation Corps) during its operation.

evidence.supports: Old Fairview Nursery lies directly across Highway 7
evidence.quote: Directly across Hwy. 7 is the site of the old Fairview Nursery.
It was organized on February 12, 1939 for Company #746 (Project #F-30).

evidence.supports: Nursery site has many existing foundations
Parking area is the access point for the Ozark Highlands Trail
evidence.quote: Access Entrance to OHT from Parking Area
The Big Piney Ranger District is considering decommissioning the Fairview Compground as per letter dated 6/13/14.

evidence.supports: Tower site recorded as a historical archaeological site
evidence.quote: has been recorded as an historical archaeological site

evidence.supports: Site in Newton County, Ozark National Forest
Managing forest is the Ozark National Forest

corrections.why: The hiking-club page calls the place a former fire tower site, now a campground.

sources.title: Fairview Campground & Historic CCC Nursery Site

notes_for_editor: Thin record: one hobbyist-club page with the site history, and a header-only lookout page. No build or removal dates and no Ozark National Forest page found. The club page's 'former fire tower' wording is the only source for the tower site; verify with the Ozark National Forest (Big Piney Ranger District). The 2014 decommission proposal may have been carried out, so the campground's current status needs checking. Brief status 'unknown' corrected to removed. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the story no longer calls the fee current (the page is undated; the latest dated note is 2014), and it reports the page's archaeological-site record for the tower site rather than saying nothing remains.
